title: Great Zimbabwe
objective: After this level you can describe the stone city of Great Zimbabwe and its trade.
summary: Ancestors of the Shona built Great Zimbabwe's mortarless stone walls and grew rich on gold trade with the Indian Ocean coast; colonial-era claims of foreign builders were false.

cards.headline: A whole country is named after a medieval city of stone.
cards.body: Zimbabwe takes its name from a Shona word meaning “stone houses”. The ruins that inspired it were once the heart of a kingdom. Who built them? For decades, some people refused to accept the answer.

cards.headline: Walls without mortar
cards.body: Great Zimbabwe was built by the ancestors of the Shona people and flourished between the 11th and 15th centuries, home at its height to 10,000 to 20,000 people. Its Great Enclosure is the largest ancient structure in sub-Saharan Africa. The granite walls stand about 10 metres high in places, laid in careful layers without mortar. Nothing holds them up but skill and gravity.

cards.headline: Gold for the world
cards.body: The city grew rich on cattle, crops and trade in gold with the coast of the Indian Ocean. Archaeologists digging there have found goods from far away: Syrian glass, Chinese celadon dishes and Persian bowls. Chinese dishes on a Shona table: that’s how far the gold reached.

cards.headline: The wrong answers
cards.body: Late 19th-century Europeans refused to credit Africans. One linked the ruins to the Queen of Sheba, another to Phoenicians or Arabians. None of it was true. In 1905 the archaeologist David Randall-MacIver showed the ruins were medieval and entirely African, and Gertrude Caton-Thompson confirmed it in 1929. Even so, from 1965 to 1980 Rhodesia’s ruling party censored what could be published about the site. The evidence never changed. The politics did.
cards.callout: Built by the ancestors of the Shona. Colonial-era claims otherwise were false.

learned: Ancestors of the Shona built it, 11th to 15th centuries

options.rationale: That was a false colonial-era claim.

options.rationale: It was built centuries before they arrived.

questions.explanation: Great Zimbabwe was built by the ancestors of the Shona people between the 11th and 15th centuries.

questions.prompt: Why were colonial-era claims about foreign builders of Great Zimbabwe wrong?

options.label: The ruins turned out to be modern fakes
Excavations showed the city was medieval and African
The Shona had written records naming the architect
The Phoenicians never used stone
options.rationale: The proof came from excavation, not that.

questions.explanation: Randall-MacIver (1905) and Caton-Thompson (1929) showed the ruins were medieval and of African origin.

questions.prompt: Great Zimbabwe’s ruins held Chinese dishes and Syrian glass. What did Level 9’s Byzantine objects at Sutton Hoo reveal about Anglo-Saxon England?

options.label: It traded gold with the Indian Ocean
It was connected to a wider world
It was cut off from the rest of Europe

questions.explanation: Goods from far away mark wide connections: Sutton Hoo showed a rich, skilled England connected to a wider world.
